title: Why Does Popcorn Pop? 4x Your Car Tire's Pressure 🍿
description:
Why does popcorn pop? Water inside each kernel turns to steam, pressure builds to about 135 psi behind the hard hull, and at around 180°C it bursts and the starch puffs into foam up to 40 times bigger.

Sources:
https://www.popcorn.org/All-About-Popcorn/What-Makes-Popcorn-Pop
https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/explore-the-pop-in-popcorn
https://www.sciencebuddies.org/stem-activities/explore-the-pop-in-popcorn

Animated in the Claymation Set style.
pinned_comment: Be honest: do you eat the unpopped kernels at the bottom of the bowl, or leave them? 👇
script: Your popcorn explodes at about 4 times, your car tire's pressure. Every kernel hides a bit of water, about 14 percent, packed in soft starch, locked inside a hard shell called the hull. Heat it up, and that water turns to steam. But the hull barely leaks, so steam has nowhere to go. Pressure climbs to about 135 pounds per square inch. Then, at around 180 degrees Celsius, the hull cracks. The starch blasts out and puffs into foam, up to 40 times bigger. And the pop you hear? That's not the shell breaking. It's the steam escaping. The first bit of starch forms a little leg, flinging the kernel into the air. Those duds in your bowl were too dry to build pressure. So, do you eat the ones that didn't explode?
key_facts: Popcorn needs about 14% moisture to pop
Pressure reaches about 135 psi before the hull bursts (popcorn.org), roughly 4x a 30-35 psi car tire
Can swell to 40-50 times its size (popcorn.org)
The pop sound comes from vapor release, not the hull cracking (Scientific American)
First starch forms a leg that catapults the kernel (popcorn.org)
Too-dry kernels don't build enough pressure
